pageCache.text:
Where Talent Meets Opportunity: Claremont's Award-Winning Performing Arts Programme
Parents know that choosing the right school for a child who loves performing arts is never simple
You want a place where your child can grow with confidence, but you also need reassurance that their education will be academically strong, broad, and future-focused.
Claremont offers that balance: specialist creative training within a full independent school, so your child does not have to choose between excellence in the classroom and excellence on stage.
More Than a School Play: What Makes a Specialist Performing Arts Programme Different
What separates a genuine specialist performing arts education from standard drama or music lessons is depth, expertise, and purpose. At Claremont, students learn from professional practitioners with real-world experience, work towards formal qualifications at every level, and train in purpose-built facilities designed to support serious development. Just as importantly, they are treated as emerging professionals, with high expectations, real responsibility, and a culture where performing arts is integrated into school life rather than added on as an extra.
Three Disciplines, One Exceptional Programme
Claremont’s programme brings together drama, dance, and music in one cohesive offer, available both as formal academic subjects and as enrichment opportunities that help every student grow. From Prep through Sixth Form, the programme is led by industry practitioners who understand how to nurture technique, confidence, and creativity at every stage. That commitment has earned Claremont national recognition, including double Independent School Association Award wins for Performing Arts. You do not need to arrive at a specialist level to benefit; this is a programme that develops young people from any starting point, helping each child discover what they can achieve.
Professional-Standard Facilities That Inspire Excellence
Claremont’s performing arts spaces are designed to do more than support lessons. They help students think and work like emerging artists. The 220-seat theatre gives young performers the chance to experience lighting, sound, audience response, and stagecraft in a setting that feels authentic, while the purpose-built dance studio and dedicated music suite create the kind of focused environment where technique can truly develop. Students rehearse, record, perform, and are assessed in professional settings, not repurposed halls, which makes a real difference to confidence and standards. They also benefit from workshops led by industry professionals and visits to external venues, including Pineapple Studios, broadening their understanding of what excellent performance training looks like beyond school.
Real Qualifications, Real Destinations
For parents, outcomes matter and Claremont’s programme is built with that in mind. Students work towards recognised qualifications through LAMDA as well as formal academic pathways, so their progress is measured and meaningful at every stage. That combination of training and achievement helps open doors, with Claremont students regularly gaining entry to specialist schools and colleges including Mountview, RADA, Performers and Bird. It is serious preparation for the next step, not just hobby-level enrichment.
Boarding Options for Dedicated Young Performers
Claremont also offers full and weekly boarding from age 10, giving dedicated young performers the stability and structure they need to thrive. For families balancing busy schedules or travelling commitments, this creates a practical way for students to combine specialist training with boarding life in a supportive environment. The daily routine is carefully organised to support both academic progress and creative development, helping students stay focused, build independence, and make the most of every opportunity.
Developing the Whole Person, Not Just the Performer
At Claremont, performing arts is about shaping the whole person, not only polishing a set of stage skills. Students bring their interests, cultures, experiences, and values into the room, and those influences become part of their creative work. They are encouraged to develop as artists with perspective, not just as performers who follow instruction. Alongside technical growth, they build camaraderie and self-reliance, learning how to collaborate with others while also trusting their own voice. They are treated as professionals, and over time, they grow into professionals. This balance of care, challenge, and expectation leaves students feeling supported and empowered.
Why Parents Choose Claremont for Performing Arts
Choosing the right school is one of the most important decisions you will make for your child, especially when their passion runs as deeply as performing arts. If you want a community that understands that passion and nurtures it seriously, come and see Claremont for yourself. Visit the facilities, meet the team, and watch the students in action.

Frequently Asked Questions
Curious about Claremont School in East Sussex? Explore our FAQs for key insights and feel free to reach out to our team for more details.
What is the Performing Arts programme at Claremont School?
It is a specialist programme covering drama, dance, and music, available from Prep through Sixth Form. It is led by industry practitioners and offers both formal academic pathways and enrichment opportunities. It has also won multiple Independent School Association Awards for Performing Arts.
What qualifications can students achieve through the Performing Arts programme?
Students work towards recognised LAMDA qualifications as well as formal academic pathways. These qualifications are measured and meaningful at every stage and help prepare students for entry into specialist schools such as Mountview, RADA, Performers and Bird.Claremont School is located in East Sussex, with two separate campuses for its Prep and Senior Schools. Close to Hastings, it is easily accessible from surrounding areas. Its beautiful Prep campus combines historic charm with modern facilities, creating an inspiring place to learn and grow, whilst the Senior School is often described as a ‘little village’ with its distinctive layout supporting a cosy, nurturing learning environment.
Excellent transport links through our bus network make the school convenient for families throughout the county and beyond. For more information, see the Our Campus and Transport pages.
Is there a performing arts boarding option at Claremont?
Yes, Claremont offers full and weekly boarding from age 10. This provides the structure and support needed to combine specialist training with academic study and personal development.
Do students need to be at a specialist level to join the programme?
No, students do not need to arrive at a specialist level. The programme supports young people from any starting point and helps each child develop their abilities and confidence over time.

Scholarships and bursaries
Families can request financial aid to access Claremont's diverse and forward-thinking tuition through bursaries or by applying for scholarships based on merits.
Available scholarships
Bursaries
Scholarships
Bursaries
Independent education represents a significant investment for families and our bursaries are awarded up to 30% of tuition fees. All bursary applications are means tested and handled by an external agency prior to a recommendation being made.Scholarships and Discretionary Bursaries can both be ‘topped up’ by a means tested bursary. Parents applying for a means tested bursary will be required to complete financial disclosure forms at the same time as any Scholarship application. A decision will be made by the Headmaster in consultation with the Principal.
Scholarships
Students entering Year 7, Year 9 and Sixth Form can apply for a scholarship. These awards are made to individuals who demonstrate outstanding potential in one or more of the following areas: sport, creative and performing arts and academic subject areas.
Scholarships information packs
Year 7 Scholarship pack
Year 9 Scholarship pack
Sixth Form Scholarship pack
Frequently Asked Questions
What is a scholarship?
A scholarship is the recognition of academic, sporting, or artistic excellence, following assessment by Claremont School.
Scholars receive a reduction on school fees, opportunities to develop further in the areas that a scholarship is awarded, and, most importantly, tailored coaching and support in the respective areas of the award offered.
How much is a scholarship award worth?
Scholarships tend to be awarded to a maximum of 15% of tuition fees.
What is a difference between a scholarship and a bursary?
Both give financial assistance but are completely separate in their assessment.
Scholarship awards are given to pupils who have demonstrated excellence and ability in their chosen scholarship area.
A bursary can be given in recognition of financial need and can be applied for on behalf of any pupil who is registered with the School, regardless of ability. A bursary can also supplement a scholarship award amount. Bursaries are means-tested, so parents are asked to complete a financial circumstances form which is then assessed by the Principal.
What is the point of a scholarship?
Being awarded a scholarship is an honour for a student that will stay with them for life. It also allows them to access special programmes in each discipline with specialist teaching, trips and opportunities available to scholars that are not available to others.
What are the fees for applying for a scholarship?
In order to apply for a Year 7, Year 9 or Year 12 scholarship a non-refundable application fee of £50.00 is required.
If you wish to accept any offer that is made a £200 Registration Fee (non-refundable) and £550.00 deposit (refundable) will be required to secure a place for September 2025/26.
For international student deposits please contact the admissions team for details.
Are scholarships available for international students?
Yes, scholarships are available to all students. Awards are made for tuition fees only.

Players hone their skills in modern facilities and follow an engaging training schedule, allowing them to develop as well-rounded athletes, whilst weekly matches help to develop an elite mindset.

Regular dance showcases

In August 2024, all of our students achieved Distinctions in their examinations.

Our students have shone at prestigious venues like Hickstead, Royal Windsor and Horse of the Year Show, thanks to expert coaching from Maria Green, a seasoned UKCC level 3 coach with an impressive competition record.

Director of Performing Arts

Sarah encourages her students to create opportunities for themselves to do what they love and not to wait for others to make it happen, with empowerment on and off stage at the heart of what she does. Under her leadership, Claremont’s Performing Arts department has thrived, fostering creativity and student leadership in a vibrant and award winning Performing Arts programme.
Sarah trained as an actor at the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama (Theatre Studies – Acting BA Hons) and Manchester Metropolitan University (PGCE). After leaving Drama school Sarah was part of a Theatre company called Hot Wax, taking comedy sketch shows to Fringe Festivals throughout the UK. Sarah has worked for the National Theatre Education Department, Half Moon Young People’s Theatre and has appeared in new work for the Royal Court. Sarah believes in the power of taking risks, often saying to her students, “Just have a go…who knows what might happen!”.
Beth has been dancing since she was three years old and hasn’t stopped! First training with Redhurst School of Dance, Sussex, Beth pursued a BA Hons Dance degree at Liverpool John Moores and Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts for Dance Technique in Contemporary, Ballet and Jazz. She holds Masters credits specialising in Dance in Education from the University of Bedfordshire. Following this, she worked as a professional dancer in London working on projects involving a variety of dance styles for events including promotional work for the CCPR (representing Dance affiliations) and teaching baby ballet at the weekend. This followed her path to obtain a PGCE from Brighton University.
Beth holds a Diploma In Dance Education with the Imperial Society of Teacher of Dance in the Classical Ballet genre. She has been examining for the AQA exam board for the last 12 years for GCSE Dance. Beth has a dog called Murphy and enjoys all things creative!
Claire trained as an actor at Mountview Theatre School before specialising at the Desmond Jones School of Mime and Physical Theatre. She worked professionally for the English Shakespeare Company, Oxfordshire Touring Theatre and Young Shakespeare. Claire travelled all over the world, often being cast as energetic young boys, sprites and an array of small furry animals.
Claire used her skills in the corporate world as a facilitator and workshop leader freelancing for a variety of creative agencies including So Just Add Water, Purple Monster and Identity. Through her love of Shakespeare Claire began to work in schools running Shakespeare workshops.
Claire is a LAMDA specialist and has been teaching the syllabus for over 20 years with students from all over the world. When Claire is not at work, she can often be found at The Globe (one of her favourite places), walking her Scottie along the seafront or watching her son’s band!
Lucy trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art and earned a BA in English from the University of Sussex, specialising in Global Cinema and Staging the Renaissance. She is also a National Youth Theatre alumni. Her performance career includes Jeff Wayne’s The War of the Worlds (London) as well as other performances in the UK and USA. Previously, Lucy won the one-minute round at MonologueSlam and co-created Proving It, a two-woman show at Theatre By The Lake. Her theatre company, Big Blanket Productions, has received multiple nominations at the Manchester Fringe Awards, including Best Play, Best Director and Best Actor for This Wide Night.
Lucy works as a voice actor and is best known for her role as Rhaya in the award-winning sci-fi audiobook The Dex Legacy. Her industry experience includes behind-the-scenes roles, such as script reader for Sky Arts and operational and backstage work for the BBC, ITV and The Royal Albert Hall.
Natasha studied Creative Music Production (BMus) at the University of Huddersfield, specialising in classical performance and sound design for film. Following this, she completed a Masters in Music (Composition) at the University of Nottingham. Natasha has taught Music and Music Technology for over ten years, and also has experience as a freelance record producer. A classically-trained violinist, Natasha performs regularly with the Sussex Concert Orchestra and Eastbourne Symphony Orchestra.
Aside from music, Natasha enjoys countryside walks with her family and two German Shepherds, as well as baking, archery and netball.
Rebecca has played French horn and piano from a young age, and ultimately went on to study Music at the University of Manchester. Rebecca was Head of Music at Mascalls school for eight years before taking a career break after having two children and acquiring a dog, Wilson.
Rebecca is passionate about ensemble playing and is Chairperson of Penshurst Choral Society, principal horn of Bacchus Wind Orchestra, plays regularly with Penshurst Brass Quintet and sings with The 1839 Consort.

pageCache.pageTitle: Claremont A Level and BTEC Students Celebrate First Choice Success
pageCache.text:
Claremont A Level and BTEC Students Celebrate First Choice Success
Claremont School is celebrating excellent A Level and BTEC results, with students securing places at a diverse range of destinations.
Claremont School is celebrating excellent A Level and BTEC results, with students securing places at a diverse range of destinations. The results reflect not only strong academic achievement, but the breadth of pathways Claremont opens up for every student, regardless of their starting point. Students taking our BTEC qualifications in 2026 have achieved over 2 grades higher than that predicted by aptitude testing, which is testament to their hard work and the personalised support each student receives in our Sixth Form.
This year's cohort is going on to pursue courses spanning the sciences, humanities, creative arts and vocational disciplines, a reflection of the School's commitment to nurturing individual strengths rather than a single definition of success. Destinations in this cycle are Law and Biological Sciences at Surrey, Politics at Exeter, Film & TV Production at Falmouth, Psychology at UCL, Architecture at Kingston, Acting at LMA and a media apprenticeship. From competitive Russell Group offers to specialist vocational routes, Claremont students are moving forward into higher education and employment with genuine confidence in the direction they have chosen. Over 90% of our students have reached their first choice of destination in 2026, which is a remarkable achievement in today's increasingly competitive market for school leavers.
"These results are a testament to the hard work of our students and the dedication of our staff," commented the school’s Principal, Ed Dickie. "But what makes us proudest is not simply the grades themselves, it's what they represent: the success of young people who have each had their own journey of discovery.”
Claremont School has long believed that qualifications alone are not enough to guarantee success in today's rapidly changing educational and workplace environment. As employers increasingly prioritise adaptability, resilience and character alongside technical knowledge, the School has placed equal emphasis on developing the skills and attitudes that allow students to turn academic achievement into lasting career success. Through its five pillars, performing arts programme and football academy, combined with alongside a rigorous academic curriculum, Claremont equips students with the confidence, curiosity and work ethic that universities and employers alike value so highlyare looking for.
“A holistic approach is central to what Claremont does best: identifying potential early, providing a platform for ambition, and supportingensuring that every student, whatever their starting point, in finding is able to find a pathway that is genuinely their own. The School's results this year are a clear demonstration of that philosophy in action.”
With the landscape of higher education and employment continuing to evolve, Claremont remains committed to preparing students not just to meet the demands of today's world, but to shape their own futures within it. The School's approach recognises that success looks different for every individual, and that a truly excellent education is one that can flex to support each student's unique ambitions.
Claremont extends its congratulations to every student receiving results this year, and to the staff and families who have supported them throughout their journey. The School looks forward to following their progress as they take the next step, whether that is at university, in an apprenticeship, or in the world of work.
For more information about Claremont, book a tour or contact the Admissions office at admissions@claremontschool.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Rising Stars - Outstanding GCSE Results at Claremont
pageCache.text:
Rising Stars - Outstanding GCSE Results at Claremont
Claremont School students celebrate outstanding GCSE results, with rising value added and improvements across every measure.
This year's cohort has delivered a very strong collective performance, with a significant rise in both the school's value added score and grade average, confirming that Claremont students are not simply achieving good grades, but consistently exceeding expectations relative to their starting points. Crucially, the improvement was not confined to a single headline figure: attainment, progress and the proportion of students achieving top grades all rose in step, reflecting a year of sustained hard work across every subject and every year group.
As ever, there are stories of individual success. For some it was achieving grade averages between 7.5 and 8.5. For others it was achieving 4s and 5s in areas where they thought they could never achieve. Success is relative and the school is proud of each and every student who has taken exams this summer. This summer has seen particular strength in Maths, English Language, Geography and PE, with Claremont’s traditional success in the Performing and Creative Arts once again replicated with outstanding grades.
Behind the numbers are hundreds of individual stories of ambition rewarded. This year's results have taken this cohort of students one step closer to a range of future careers: future doctors securing the grades that keep them on the path to medicine, engineers edging towards building the next generation of technology, dancers and artists growing in confidence and skill as they explore their creative boundaries. GCSEs are the first key academic landmark for children growing up and, whatever the final destination, Claremont's Y11 can leave this results day with real momentum as they head into the Sixth Form.
The School’s Principal, Ed Dickie commented: “What strikes me most about this year's results is not just the grades themselves, but the attitude that produced them. It has been a fabulous Y11. Our students have shown extraordinary ambition and resilience, and that spirit is exactly what will carry them through their next step into Sixth Form education. In a flash they will be choosing university, apprenticeship or career options; today, they are all one step closer to that moment and in a stronger place than they were yesterday. They now know more about who they are and what they can achieve.”
Claremont’s distinct learning approach emphasises the development of life skills and the opportunities that come outside the classroom as well as inside it. It will be these skills and experiences that turn great qualifications into successful lives and careers. Staff across the school have pointed to a genuine culture shift in recent times, with students taking greater ownership of their learning and setting their own ambitious targets. That drive, combined with high-quality teaching and a relentless focus on progress for every individual, has translated directly into results that speak for themselves.
As students celebrate today, the school is already looking ahead, with plans in place to build on this year's momentum and ensure the next cohort is given every opportunity to again take their own step closer to success.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Claverham Community College
I am delighted to welcome you to our College website, which offers an insight into the life, ethos, and achievements of our school.
At Claverham Community College, we provide students with a high-quality, broad, and ambitious education, enabling them to reach their full potential in a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment. Our curriculum, pastoral care, and enrichment programmes are designed to foster a love of learning, resilience, and personal responsibility, while promoting the College’s core values of Ambition, Integrity, Independence, Respect, and Resilience.
We are committed to developing students who, through determination and effort, achieve the highest levels of academic and personal development. Equally, we place great emphasis on consideration for others, polite and respectful behaviour, and positive contributions to our local and wider community. Our aim is to nurture responsible, community-minded, and globally aware young people who are prepared to shape the future.
Our success is underpinned by a distinct philosophy: high expectations, hard work, traditional values, strong relationships, and recognition of each individual’s worth. This approach has contributed to consistently strong academic outcomes and was recognised in our 2023 Ofsted inspection, where inspectors praised the college for pupils’ pride, resilience, and positive attitudes, as well as for the quality of leadership, collaboration, and staff engagement.
Claverham is more than a school. Our 42-acre campus is home to a recently opened state-of-the-art teaching wing, a vibrant Sports Centre, and Battle Day Nursery, all of which provide outstanding facilities that benefit both students and the wider community. We take pride in being at the heart of Battle and the surrounding villages, serving a diverse catchment and fostering strong connections with families and local organisations.
We hope you find our website helpful and informative. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you would like to learn more about the College, its values, or the opportunities available to our students and community.
Mr. P SwattonPrincipal.
Exam Results
The achievements of our students this year are a testament to their resilience, dedication, and hard work. As a College, we place great importance on the academic and personal growth of our students, and we are immensely proud of the accomplishments of this group of young adults.
Many of our students have delivered outstanding individual performances, including those who have earned the highest possible grades. Just as rewarding, however, has been celebrating the success of those who have made exceptional progress throughout their time at Claverham.
Our heartfelt congratulations go to all of the young people who have achieved such impressive results, which will undoubtedly serve as a foundation for their future success. These achievements reflect the commitment and dedication of both students and staff, as well as the unwavering support of parents and governors.
As always, we will continue to build on this success, striving to provide the excellent education that all of our students deserve.

Admissions
We are delighted that you are considering Claverham Community College as the secondary school of choice for your child.
Claverham Community College accepts students in Years 7 to 11.
Choosing the right secondary school for your child is a big decision and we know that many parents who live in Battle and its surrounding area start actively exploring all available schools for their child at an early stage.
On this page we have included a number of documents which will hopefully help you with your decision-making process.
Each year we hold an open evening and a number of open mornings whereby prospective parents and students can see the college in operation.
In-year admissions (where a student is admitted part way through the academic year) are sometimes possible, but please be aware that Claverham Community College is generally oversubscribed in most year groups so it may, subject to circumstances, be necessary to join a waiting list.
For information on the availability of places for in-year admissions please contact Mrs Taylor. In-year admission applications are processed by East Sussex County Council.
If your child is due to join Year 7 in a secondary school in September 2026, you will need to apply by 31st October 2025.
To apply for a school place please use the link below;https://www.eastsussex.gov.uk/education-learning/schools/apply-for-a-school-place
What happens if you apply late
If you apply after the closing date, the request will be dealt with after all on-time preferences have been processed. This may affect your chances of securing a preferred school.
If you move into the area after the closing date you should apply for a school place as soon as possible. Please contact the East Sussex Admissions Team on;
Phone: 0300 33 09 472 between 10 am to 3 pm Monday to FridayEmail: admissions@eastsussex.gov.uk
What to expect
If you apply online, you will receive an email to confirm the admissions team received your application.
You can sign in to view your account at any time.
If you have sent a paper form it is your responsibility to check the admissions team have received this.
Offer of a place
Decisions are sent on the national offer day. We won’t give an early decision under any circumstances.
The Local Authority sends decisions on allocation day by email if you applied online, or by letter if not.
If you did not get the school(s) you wanted for your child, the decision letter will explain your options.
If you are successful in being offered a place at Claverham Community College we will be in touch shortly after the allocation date.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Absence
It is a legal requirement to inform the College if a pupil is going to be absent or will be arriving late for any reason (medical, interview etc.). Without an e-mail or use of Arbor our staff would have no way of knowing whether an absence was due to your child not being sent to school or being sent and not arriving.
REPORTING A CHILD’S ABSENCE OR LATE ARRIVAL
If your child is unwell or going to be late into school for any reason, for their safety, please contact the school before 08:30.
Absences need to be reported daily by email or through the Arbor parent app. Medical evidence can be requested at any time. This evidence could be in the form of a compliment slip, appointment card, copy of prescription, prescribed medicinal packaging or a doctor’s note. Parents can be fined by ESCC if medical evidence is not provided.
All pupils who arrive late to school or need to leave early for any reason must report to Reception to sign in, or out, as appropriate.
If your child returns to school after an illness and you would like to inform us that your child has been sent, please contact the College using the above contact details so that we can alert you if your child does not arrive at school as expected. Please contact us again on Monday morning if your child’s illness continues into a second week.
For the latest guidance on Covid-19 please check the Government website here here
Medical Appointments
I would ask parents to give the College advanced notice of medical appointments where these cannot be arranged outside school hours. If a medical appointment requires your child to leave during the school day a letter from you is still required and needs to be handed to your child’s House Tutor for signature at morning registration on the day of the appointment, this letter needs to be handed to reception when signing out as confirmation that they have permission to leave. I understand it is not always possible to make medical appointments out of school hours but appreciate your efforts in keeping the amount of missed time to a minimum.
The Department for Education (DfE) has amended the regulations and guidance in relation to absences in term-time. There is no automatic right to take your child out of school during term time. From 1st September 2013, government legislation no longer enables head teachers to authorise requests for leave for children to be taken out of school unless there are considered to be exceptional circumstances. More information can be found in the following documents.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cradle Hill Community Primary School - Breakfast and After School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School
Kittiwakes
At Cradle Hill Community Primary School we offer parents flexible care wrapped around the school day through our Kittiwakes Club.
Our club is run and administered by our staff who also work in the school during the day so they are known to both children and parents. They are a dedicated team of professionals who focus on the children's need to relax, play and have a choice in what they do.
We offer a range of activities, including craft, indoor and outdoor games, reading, imaginary play and construction. During their time at Kittiwakes Club children can choose activities that suit them best.
The Club is open to all children from Reception to Year 6 and aims to provide a safe, secure and relaxed environment for the children in our care where they can be happy.
From January 2024 our opening times and prices are:
Breakfast Club 7:45am – 8.45am £3.50
After school Club Session 1: 3.15pm – 4.30pm £4.50
After school club Session 2: 4.30pm - 5.30pm £4.00
A full afternoon session (3.15pm - 5.30pm) will cost £8.50
Children are provided with breakfast in the morning. We offer toast and a choice of butter, jam or marmite and a range of cereals such as, multigrain hoops, weetabix, shreddies, rice crispies and cornflakes. Apple juice, milk and water are also provided.
In the afternoon, they have a hot or cold snack.
Sessions should be booked via our online booking system. Log ins will be provided by the School Office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cradle Hill Community Primary School - Children as Leaders
pageCache.text:
Children as Leaders
Leadership Opportunities
At Cradle Hill Primary School, we recognise that our children are the leaders of the future and therefore provide a range of opportunities for children to develop their leadership skills. Pupil voice is valued and promoted – each academic year, pupils are given a platform to express the views of their school to help shape its development. We encourage all of our pupils to embrace the wide range of opportunities available to them – and always seek to find new ways that we can further empower our pupils. This enables our pupils to develop as individuals, as a community and grow the school as a whole.
Leadership Roles
House Captains: Voted for by their houses – Anne Frank, Nightingale, Einstein and Shakespeare. To become a House Captain, children must submit a video outlining why they would be a good representative for their house.
School Parliament: Members are voted for by their classes after a short presentation. The focus of our School Parliament is to help make sure the children's voices are heard with regard to the curriculum, the school environment and after school activities.
Reading Champions: Children in Key Stage 2 are invited to apply for the job of Reading Champion by filling out an application form. These are reviewed by our Reading Champions Lead, Mrs Dower, who selects 12 children to join her passionate team. The Reading Champions meet monthly to discuss how reading can be improved in our school.
Eco Warriors: Eco Warriors strive to ensure our school and local community is as eco-friendly as possible! They ​meet weekly to learn about the world, monitor energy use and come up with new initiatives to help keep our planet happy and engage their community. ​They also host assemblies to support the growth of our eco mindset.
Play Leaders: Our Play Leaders completed 2 days of training and have all received their 'play makers' award. The training focused on the four core areas of play leadership – Participants, Area, Communication and Equipment . The play leaders role is to run games and activities for other children during break times, with the aim of making playtimes more active, inclusive and fun!

pageCache.pageTitle: Cradle Hill Community Primary School - PSHE and RSHE
pageCache.text:
PSHE and RSHE
Intent
At Cradle Hill School the PSHE/RSHE curriculum, known as 'Let's Talk’, will prepare children to live in an increasingly complex world which presents both positive and exciting opportunities as well as challenges and risk.
It will achieve this by helping them develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they will need to manage their lives now and in the future.
By the time they leave Cradle Hill School children will have an essential understanding of how to stay healthy.
They will be taught about the concept of mental wellbeing and how to take care of themselves and receive support if mental health issues arise. They will understand the key building blocks of respectful relationships that focus on family and friends in all contexts, including on line. They will be skilled in managing their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way and know how to manage their personal safety by assessing and handling risk. They will be prepared to make the most of life and work and live in the wider world.
The curriculum has been written in consultation with parents/carers and the wider community in line with statutory requirements. All information about this consultation is available on our website.
Implementation
'Let's Talk' comprehensively covers the statutory guidance outlining the content that schools must cover from September 2020. (See the DfE publication ‘Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education’. In addition, it includes non-statutory aspects of the PSHE curriculum that the document does not mention such as economic well-being, careers and enterprise education and personal safety, including assessing and managing risk.
To achieve this, the curriculum is delivered through the following six core themes:
The core themes are taught through well-chosen, carefully sequenced units (contexts) that will allow pupils to embed new knowledge so that it can be confidently used in real life situations. The themes also facilitate the revisiting, reinforcing and extending of prior learning so that knowledge, skills, related vocabulary and attributes are developed year upon year. Whilst the themes are separate, a lot of content will overlap. In particular, relationships and assessing and managing risk and managing life online are integrated throughout all three themes.
All subject content will be delivered in an age appropriate and developmentally appropriate way, taking into consideration pupils’ increasing independence and physical social awareness as they move through the school.
The curriculum will be taught sensitively and inclusively with respect to the backgrounds and beliefs of pupils and parents, while always with the aim of providing pupils with the knowledge they need of the law.
Core theme 1: Resilience
Core theme 2: Relationships
Core theme 3: Well-Being
Core theme 4: Health Education
Core theme 5: Friendships
Core theme 6: Wider World
Impact
Our PSHE curriculum is planned to demonstrate skills, knowledge and vocabulary progression to ensure age related attainment at the end of each Key Stage. Upon completion of each unit teachers will assess children against the progression of skills and knowledge document.
Assessment is in relation to each of the core themes:
Termly assessment will take place to track children’s progress against age related expectations for PSHE.

pageCache.text:
Spanish (MFL)
Intent
At Cradle Hill we believe that the learning of a foreign language provides a valuable educational, social and cultural experience for our pupils. It helps them to develop their ability to communicate, including key skills of speaking and listening and extends their knowledge of how language works. It provides excitement, enjoyment and challenge for children, helping to create enthusiastic learners and to develop positive attitudes to language learning throughout life. Learning another language gives children a new perspective on the world, encouraging them to understand their own cultures and those of others. The natural links between languages and other areas of the curriculum can enrich the overall teaching and learning experience.
Implementation
At Cradle Hill we endeavour to integrate language learning into everyday school life, with teachers, teaching assistants and children using and experimenting with their knowledge of different languages whenever the opportunity arises. We foster a problem-solving approach, giving children opportunities to work out language use for themselves in a supportive context where risk-taking and creativity are encouraged, and there is an emphasis on having fun with the new language. From Years 3 to Year 6 children will have specific skills, concepts and vocabulary in a weekly dedicated lesson with a specialist Spanish teacher.

Governors
What is the role of the Governing Body?
The Governing Body at Cradle Hill Community Primary School works in partnership with the staff to promote high quality education for pupils.
We appoint the Head Teacher and work closely with them to make decisions that directly affect the education and well-being of all children.
Part of a school's governing body's responsibilities are to:
The Governing Body is a 'critical friend', challenging and supporting the Senior Leadership Team, monitoring the outcome of policies and ensuring accountability.
Promote high standards of educational attainment
Set an annual budget detailing planned spending
How is the Governing Body organised?
The Chair of our Full Governing Body is Iain Day and the Vice-Chair of the Full Governing Body is Paul Amos. Our Governing Body is organised into two committees to support in the running of the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cradle Hill Community Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Intent
Our music curriculum aims to provide a passionate, engaging experience where children will be immersed in a celebration of different genres of inspirational music from around the world, then use their broadening knowledge and listening skills to develop as musicians and performers.
They will understand that some music can be meaningful with a powerful message, yet other music will capture an emotion- then learn how to create their own music reflecting this understanding.
As well as celebrating world culture through music, they will uncover some of the rich folk heritage of this area, learning to sing local smuggler’s songs that would have been sung here hundreds of years ago.
When creating and performing their own music, children will feel safe to explore, understanding that making mistakes and developing perseverance will make them a better musician, and being given the knowledge and tools to progress to the next level of musical learning, becoming ever more independent.
Children will learn to play both traditional and electronic musical instruments, using them to develop composing skills culminating in writing their own leaver’s song celebrating their unique identity.
Ultimately, we want the broadening of our children’s understanding of other cultures and histories together with the development of their own sensitivity, creativity and confidence to lay a foundation for a musical journey that will continue throughout their lives.
Implementation
At Cradle Hill, we are lucky to have a well- stocked and spacious Music Room, with many instruments including five keyboards, Xylophones and Glockenspiels and 30 Ukuleles as well as a large selection of non- pitched instruments. The interactive displays in the music room allow children to write their honest opinions in the feedback and suggestion box, which informs the planning for the music curriculum the following year.
Music is taught through a combination of Charanga Music School, Sing Up and Out of the Ark, supplemented in KS2 by Ten Pieces, all of which are designed to give children opportunities to develop active listening skills, knowledge of genres and historical periods, singing and instrumental techniques, improvising and composing skills, notation, vocabulary and musical dimension understanding, and performance skills. As children progress through the school, they revisit appropriately sequenced musical knowledge, skills and vocabulary so that they are built on year-by-year. This ensures children are given opportunities to achieve depth in their learning.
Children begin to explore chime bars, basic xylophones and non-pitched percussion instruments in KS1, then move onto chromatic Glockenspiels and Ukuleles in KS2.
In Y2 children begin to learn electronic music skills, using Chrome Music Lab; then begin to use Garageband in Y4, extending to Quickbeats in Y6, which they can practise at home using to Yumu, a safe music platform which is part of Charanga Music School, where they can explore and compose backing beats, as well as develop their end of year compositions on identity.
Singing is very important to our school - we have separate singing assemblies every week and a very popular choir which even ran (outside!) during lockdown. The choir takes part in the One Voice Festival of Singing, where they perform with other primary schools alongside the Glyndebourne Chorus, as well as singing carols every year to Threeways, a local Nursing Home.
Ongoing feedback and continual encouragement and support is given to each pupil on this musical journey, who will leave our school with a clear idea of their own musical preferences; the confidence to compose, play, sing and perform with increasing musicality.
Impact
We believe that musical learning is not necessarily a linear process but a journey which differs for every child.
Therefore, while incremental progression develops in each year group leading to a defined end point at the end of each key stage, we assess holistically, over the pupil’s entire time at Cradle Hill.
We use multiple sources, such as recording responses to songs; instrumental skills; singing ability; improvising and composing skills; ability to work in or lead a group; ability to make meaningful marks which relate to sounds; performance skills and ability to edit and critically their own and other pupil’s work, to gather information.
Ongoing feedback and continual encouragement and support is given to each pupil on this journey, who leaves our school with a clear idea of their own musical preferences; the confidence to compose, play, sing and perform with increasing musicality, and above all, a genuine love of music which they will carry with them forever.

Welcome
Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School is a deeply inclusive and welcoming school, driven by a vision that ensures every child and adult can flourish.
Our dedicated staff team is committed to nurturing the whole child, providing an inspiring environment where spiritual and academic growth go hand-in-hand. We strive to offer a transformative learning experience rooted in dignity and respect, and we hope this website captures the community and joy that defines our school family.
If you would like to find out more about Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School please contact the school office 01435 862941.
School Values
Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School has established Respect, Community, Kindness, and Perseverance as its four core Christian values to provide a moral and spiritual compass that guides every aspect of school life.
By weaving these specific values into the curriculum and daily interactions, the school provides practical, life-enhancing force that drives both academic achievement and personal wellbeing.
Thrive
Thrive Approach is a tangible expression of "Dignity and Respect," as it treats each child as a unique individual made in the image of God, providing bespoke support. It bridges the gap between the school's theological values and practical mental health support.

Clubs
At Cross in Hand we aim to provide a range of clubs during term time. Whilst some may run throughout the year, others may only run for a specified time. We would encourage all pupils to participate and try the clubs on offer. Most clubs offered are organised by outside agencies while some teachers have their own areas of expertise and interest and offer additional opportunities for pupils in these areas.
When the children join a club, we expect commitment from them and if they cannot attend, it is their responsibility to notify the teacher running the club. If a child decides they do not want to continue with a club, they should also tell the teacher to allow that space to be taken by another child as there is often a waiting list. We expect the same high standards of behaviour in clubs as we do in school and so we make pupils aware that if their behaviour falls short of this, they may lose their space and their parents will be notified.
A letter about clubs on offer is sent out at the start of each term.

pageCache.pageTitle: crossinhand.org - Yoto Project
pageCache.text:
Yoto Project
Reading sits at the heart of every child’s learning journey. Strong reading skills open the door to the full curriculum, building confidence, curiosity, and a lifelong love of learning. From the earliest years, we prioritise creating joyful, meaningful reading experiences for all our pupils.
Our Yoto Project brings this vision to life by pairing older and younger children through the magic of storytelling. Older pupils record captivating audio versions of favourite books, which are then turned into bespoke Yoto cards. Younger children listen to these recordings while following along in their own copies, strengthening both comprehension and enthusiasm for reading.
To ensure everyone in Reception, Year 1 & Year 2 can take part, Yoto players and book sets rotate around the children. This simple but powerful routine helps foster connection, independence, and a shared love of stories throughout our school community.
Reception, Year 1 & Year 2
Children will take it in turn to take home the Yoto player and the books and they will be able to listen to older children reading their favourite stories as the follow along in the books.
Thanks to the Friends of Cross in Hand School for funding this project.

RSHE is taught across the school using a scheme called Jigsaw: The Mindful Approach to RSHE. Jigsaw teaches children to become aware of their thoughts and feelings, as they happen, helping them to concentrate, focus and regulate their emotional states.
It covers the following 'puzzles' or units of work: Being Me in My World, Celebrating Difference, Dreams & Goals, Healthy Me, Relationships and Changing Me. This last ‘puzzle’ is where we teach our Sex and Relationships Education (SRE).

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome - The Sabden Multi Academy Trust
pageCache.text:
Welcome
My name is David Donnelly, Principal of Cuckmere House School, and I would like to extend a warm welcome to our website. The aim of this platform is to keep you informed of the latest news and information regarding our exceptional school. We take immense pride in ensuring the best outcomes for our students and I hope this website provides you with a glimpse of how we nurture our students towards success.
Cuckmere House School is an outstanding special school catering to children and young people with social, emotional, and mental health (SEMH) needs from Key Stage 1 to Key Stage 4. Our school is a unique and inspiring community, dedicated to providing each child with the highest possible standard of education while supporting them to better manage their behavioural, emotional, and mental health needs.
Our vision is to create a warm, caring, stable, and supportive environment where all pupils and staff feel safe, valued, and empowered. Through an engaging and challenging curriculum, we aim to cultivate the multitude of skills and talents our young people possess, enabling them to become independent, resilient, and self-motivated individuals who take pride in their achievements and their educational journey.
At the core of our approach lies our ‘Head, Heart, Hand’ philosophy, which shapes every aspect of our curriculum:
These principles are underpinned by our CARES values, which guide our daily interactions and long-term goals as a school community:
As Principal, I am deeply committed to building strong, trusting relationships with students, parents/carers, and our local community. These relationships are the foundation upon which a successful school thrives, ensuring that we work collaboratively to support our young people in reaching their full potential and becoming active, positive members of society.
Thank you for visiting our website. I invite you to explore further and discover how Cuckmere House School is making a meaningful difference in the lives of our students every day.
David Donnelly Principal

Careers
Careers Education, Information and Guidance at Cuckmere House School
Here at Cuckmere House School we are committed to ensuring our pupils achieve well and are fully prepared for the next steps in their education, training and employment. Many factors will contribute to how well a young person manages the transition from school to college, training or an apprenticeship. We believe that access to well-planned, up-to-date and individually tailored careers advice can make a big impact on the choices young people make and their ability to make the most of the opportunities available to them during these times. There is strong research evidence that shows that high quality careers advice will have a positive impact on learners as they move through the different stages of education and training and into the work place.
We encourage pupils to consider how their strengths and interests are compatible with different employment and career routes. We start a spiral pathway from year 7 right through to year 11, building up a careers portfolio, through CEIAG and teachers linking training, employment and apprenticeship opportunities with their subjects. We also try to make pupils aware of the career routes that would not be available to them if they opted out of particular subjects.
We have a strong focus on employability skills and attributes. Using researched based practice to inform our careers programme, we have included the six capabilities (identified by Impetus (2014) Ready for Work Impetus) in our careers programme. These are set out below:-
• Self-aware – able to take responsibility for themselves and their actions, able to control themselves and to recognise their strengths and weaknesses;
• Receptive – able to take feedback and advice, willing to address weaknesses, to learn and to try new things;
• Driven – able to see a job to its conclusion, to be punctual, well-organised and positive;
• Self-assured – willing to ask questions and seek advice, to work alone without direction, able to be confident in social situations and in their work;
• Resilient – able to cope with setbacks, rejection and criticism, determined to overcome obstacles and able to stay calm under pressure;
• Informed – knowledgeable about the job market, how to search for a job and to effectively interview; knowledgeable about how to conduct themselves in a professional environment.
More recently and in addition to this we also work towards the 8 Gatsby Benchmark for delivering careers in school.
The eight Gatsby benchmarks of Good Career Guidance
1. A stable careers programme
2. Addressing the needs of each pupil
3. Learning from career and labour market information
4. Linking curriculum learning to careers
5. Encounters with employers and employees
6. Experiences of workplaces
7. Encounters with further and higher education
8. Personal guidance
These are set out in more detail in the Gatsby Benchmarks which you can download below. Something new that we introduced from September 2018 is each pupil will have a record of each Gatsby benchmark going through secondary school with them, evidencing their individual achievements.
As the Careers Advisor for Cuckmere House School, I am responsible for ensuring all pupils understand the options they have available to them and to support them to make good choices to secure the best possible outcomes as they move through school towards the world of work. As well as teaching careers education discretely, I am also responsible for ensuring the careers input across the school is well balanced, responsive to our pupils' needs and the opportunities available locally. This includes subject based discussions, guest speakers, assembly themes, off-site visits and college and work experience opportunities.
We always welcome opportunities for our pupils to learn about different careers and working environments. If you think you could contribute in any way to support our pupils’ understanding and experiences of work, I would like to hear from you as home input plays an important part of transitioning into the work place.
Please take some time to sit with your child and have a discussion about the future. Check out some careers at Latest Issue of Make the Future Yours! — Make The Future Yours! or have a look at :
www.careerseastsussex.co.uk/information/local-industries.
5 of the biggest myths about apprenticeships busted - The Education Hub (blog.gov.uk)
Further information on SEND transition into post 16 can be found in the ESCC guide for parents and carers. Please click on the link to see the booklet Post16 Parent Carer Booklet - 1
Anne Seymour Boon – CEIAG Careers Education, Information and Guidance

signals.text: These initiatives include our Community Music Day, Get Up & Dance, our partnership with Cuckfield Bookfest, termly sports festivals, Wednesday ‘open labs’ and school Shakespeare performances among others.

With nine wide ranging ensembles each week and over 80% of Year 3 and 4 pupils playing a musical instrument, Music runs through all parts of our school and we are inordinately proud of the pupils that have gone onto win Music Scholarships to schools including King’s Canterbury, Ardingly, Brighton College and Eton.
From ballet to street dance, modern to Charleston, our weekly clubs and curriculum sessions mean Dance is part of the rhythm of everyday life at Cumnor.

Raising the bar, and drawing on her background in textile design, our dedicated Head of Art encourages children to work with a wide range of materials and processes in both 2D and 3D media, including sketching, painting, printmaking, textiles, ceramics, sculpture and animation.

Guided by our expert staff, many of whom hold regional and national honours in their own right, all children will have regular opportunities to play, within school as well as externally in local and national events, festivals and fixtures.

Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Every moment, extraordinary
Cumnor House Sussex offers an outstanding contemporary education, built on our commitment to individual opportunity, excellence and community.
We nurture individual, unique potential and believe every moment is an opportunity to unlock exciting new possibilities. Every child belongs.
Every moment, extraordinary
Every moment, extraordinary
Preparing for the future
A Cumnor education prepares children for entry into the best senior schools in the country. Broad and rich, it is distinctly contemporary in its approach, designed to ignite a love of learning and lay foundations for life.
Preparing for the future
Discover Pupil Stories
Conscientious Achiever
Conscientious Achiever
Teddy
Dramatic Presence
Teddy joined Cumnor at the beginning of Year 5 and immediately stole our hearts. Coming from a Steiner school, this amazing young woman, with her gentle smile, tangible warmth and eagerness to learn has accelerated academically. Within a few weeks, she was on the stage with a lead role in the Year 5 musical, where we realised just what talent she had modestly hidden from the world.
To hear her sing, to see her eyes light up, to feel the joy and emotion of performance flow through her is just wonderful. She’s thrown herself into everything here, and brings a sense of peace and togetherness to her friendships. But the stage remains her happy place, and we love seeing her there too.
Aggie
Competitive Spirit
Aggie is full of potential energy. Around school, she is relaxed, easy-going, affable; immensely popular, she is loved for her non-judgemental heart and her slightly goofy humour. Quietly diligent and conscientious, she has secured a place at Brighton College, testimony to her growing academic confidence and her great attitude.
But then you put her onto the sports pitch, and suddenly she transforms. Tall, athletic, powerful, she is brave, she is competitive and she exudes talent. An A team player across all the sports, she is a genuine all-rounder at this stage, as accomplished in a technical sport such as cricket or hockey, as she is on the athletics track or football pitch. And yet, despite all the medals and personal accolades, she comes off the pitch and is immediately her humble, kind and thoughtful self.
Rafe
Exceptional Mind
Rafe has been with us since Nursery, and even back then, you could tell just how bright and driven he is. He has an exceptional mind, but more than that, he loves to learn, and just loves to get better. He relishes exams and tests, embraces discussion and debate, is interested in the world around him and how it works. He loves to ask the big questions. He happens also to be quick, athletic, sporty; he is kind and sensitive, relishing his role as a peer mentor; and he doesn’t mind donning a tutu and making fun of himself on stage at a recent Variety Show!
He’s an excellent Head Boy, full of insight, empathy and practicality. Most importantly, he is a good person with great values and a humble heart.
Mia
Nurturing Spirit
It can be hard for most children to move schools, especially when you are so young, but imagine coming out of ‘lockdown’, having lived on a tropical Island, only to arrive in Sussex at a British Prep! Such has been Mia’s journey, joining us, as she did, from Mauritius in 2022.
Not surprisingly, Mia was initially tentative and shy, and found some of the formalities of the classroom hard to adjust to. Yet, through the loving care and support of her form teachers and TAs, as well as the warmth and fun of her peers, you will now find her earnestly beavering away with the broadest of grins on her face.
In fact, she is perhaps one of the most emotionally intelligent children in the year, and carries with her a deeply nurturing spirit, the first to welcome any new child into the classroom.
Hugo
Young Entrepreneur
You will struggle to find a more willing, keen, enthusiastic learner than Hugo.
He is by nature diligent and very conscientious, and given his learning needs, he continues to show great perseverance and determination in all of his academic subjects. He is flourishing in our Kudos curriculum, where he has not only been able to demonstrate his skills and knowledge in different ways, but has also found opportunities such as our Entrepreneurship program that have harnessed his creativity and social intelligence, and earnt himself some money along the way!
Cheerful, eager, full of positivity and engagement, he is a much loved boy here at Cumnor. He has a fantastic attitude to life, always willing to put up his hand and ‘have a go’; he will certainly go a long way in life.
Nakiso
Positive Presence
Nakiso arrived in 2023 as one of our Foundation Scholars. The first thing you notice about her is her smile, and wherever she is around the Cumnor campus, she exudes positivity. She never takes the opportunities on offer here at Cumnor for granted, and is utterly wholehearted in everything she does. She is strong, conscientious and engaged, with a diligent heart and mind that means that her progress in all areas of school life has been rapid.
What Nakiso loves most about Cumnor are her friends, whom she blesses with her kindness, steadiness and loyalty. All children deserve a place to put down their roots and blossom, and that is just what Nakiso is doing.
Ethan
Quiet Confidence
Ethan is a quietly impressive young man. His growth in confidence, maturity and aspiration over the past two years has been astonishing, chiefly fuelled by his love for Performing Arts.
Ethan has weekly LAMDA lessons at school, and is a prominent member of many Cumnor music groups and choirs. His main instrument is the French Horn, but he also sings and is teaching himself the piano. He has thrown himself into Cumnor productions and his growing confidence has helped him secure offers from all three of the top Sussex senior schools he applied for. Bright, creative, imaginative, sensitive, kind, determined, self-reliant, we suspect he will be a star of the stage or screen in the future.
Matilda
Conscientious Achiever
Matilda is by nature very conscientious. In the classroom, her love of reading, her creativity and imagination, and her willingness to engage in new ideas and learning really shines through. She is mature, independent, but happy to collaborate.
Matilda is a keen contributor to all areas of Cumnor life, and has already hit some notable heights, whether it be a starring role as the Headmistress in our phenomenal Year 7 production of ‘School of Rock’, or bowling the critical over at Lords, helping to secure a bronze medal in the ECB National Finals.
Enthusiastic and curious, she literally brightens a room, and has a very positive influence on those around her, full of grace and warmth.

Music
The Music Department plays an important part in school life and is dedicated to engaging and inspiring pupils, building on their natural enthusiasm.
Music at Cumnor taps into children’s natural love of music and encourages them to explore further. We focus not just on technical knowledge, but help children to build their own musical language to express their thoughts and ideas.
Through weekly music lessons in our historic Music Barn, children develop an awareness of a wide range of musical genres and eras as well as the technical and theoretical knowledge to support their performing and composing skills.
With nine wide ranging ensembles each week and over 80% of Year 3 and 4 pupils playing a musical instrument, Music runs through all parts of our school and we are inordinately proud of the pupils that have gone onto win Music Scholarships to schools including King’s Canterbury, Ardingly, Brighton College and Eton.
The results speak for themselves and we are delighted to have been shortlisted by The Week School Guide 2025 for ‘Best for Music’! To be featured alongside two cathedral schools is testament to the strength of our Department.
I am delighted to have joined Cumnor this term and I am excited to bring my many years’ experience in professional music, particularly as a pianist and Musical Director on countless national tours and West End productions, to uphold and further develop the school’s incredibly high standards of performance.
With so many schools seeing a decline in the number of pupils learning orchestral instruments, developing our choirs and orchestra is of utmost priority. Our young people are the orchestra of the future – I hope we will boast an unrivalled range of orchestral musicians in a Music Department that thrives as the beating heart of the school.
Mr Cousins, Director of Music

Our Music provision comes in many shapes in sizes. From exploring and mastering a new instrument – from piano to harp, and electric guitar to gamelan – to all types of singing, as soloists, choristers and in musical theatre.

pageCache.pageTitle: Matilda the Musical Jr Reflections | Cumnor House Sussex
pageCache.text:
Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Matilda the Musical Jr Reflections
Every so often, something happens that feels so significant, that it elicits a wide variety of responses. I’ve tried to capture some of mine.
Fergus Llewellyn, Headmaster
At Cumnor, we often talk about moments. And when we talk about moments, we think of things that individuals might experience. The excitement of a child experiencing something new. The joy of a parent witnessing their child do something amazing.
What happened in our theatre last week feels like a moment for the whole community. A collective moment where we all felt something extraordinary had just happened. A moment where deep down we all knew we had witnessed something that would be spoken of for years. A moment where everybody in that space felt transported and transformed.
There is something truly beautiful in seeing talent shine. I have said many times that I believe all of our children are unique and wonderful; to see that wonderfulness in all its power and glory is truly special, and it takes a truly special talent to draw it out.
One of the unique things about drama, especially school drama, is that it becomes a collective experience. The whole year group are involved, and the whole school comes to watch.
One of the most powerful things about Matilda the Musical Jr was the fact that every single performer, and every single performance, was of the highest standard. Every child connected – with the music, with the moment, with each other. They were all utterly in it.
The energy was palpable, the teamwork extraordinary. That sense of connection is so rare.
Matilda is a play about a young girl finding her place in the world, and how the kind, affirming encouragement of the two women in her life allow her to find her voice. And when she finds her voice, others follow. That is exactly what we witnessed last week.
What last week also confirmed for me is that leading a school well means allowing the talent you have in your team to be liberated. Our Director of Drama, Charley Harris, has always had the conviction that she could create something very special, and she was right. Alongside, we built the team. Rob Cousins, as our Director of Music, with all his West End experience, was the perfect fit, and he added so much. Sam Taylor, as a young graduate, is full of talent and creativity, and perfectly balanced the group.
Everybody sensed that something special was happening; that something very important for those children, for the school, was about to take place. Our culture, the culture of aiming high and being kind, kicked in. Tim Freeman and our Maintenance team spent countless, dedicated hours creating set design to rival professional theatres, even building a swing! Barney J, a Year 8 DT Scholar, designed, programmed and operated the incredibly technical stage lighting. Over 25 staff volunteered to help with backstage, make up, front of house, catering……the list goes on.
I am proud of each and every one of our Year 7 children, of all that they have given, of the skills they have shown, of their teamwork, their attitude, and ultimately their performance. Ultimately, how do I feel?
I feel a deep sense of joy. Joy in the effect that the performance had on all who have seen it. Joy in the fact that our community has experienced the power of theatre. Joy that I’ve been able to stand at the back of a dark room and be part of it.

Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Art and design
We value art highly at Cumnor, inspiring all our budding artists to express themselves freely, and with confidence. Our reputation for excellence is founded in nurturing individual creativity.
We are firing young imaginations, nurturing individual creativity and developing technical skills for the future.
We challenge children to develop their own, original ideas, and support them with the practical elements that enable them to become technically proficient.
Raising the bar, and drawing on her background in textile design, our dedicated Head of Art encourages children to work with a wide range of materials and processes in both 2D and 3D media, including sketching, painting, printmaking, textiles, ceramics, sculpture and animation.
A sketchbook work culture sits at the heart of our approach, encouraging everyone to keep art journals and to instil a lifelong love of drawing.
Our distinct approach is consistently recognised through the number of Art Scholarships our children have secured at a range of senior schools including Brighton College, King’s Canterbury, Tonbridge, Eastbourne and Hurst.
Kerrie Pope, Head of Art
Joined by inspirational artists and art educators, our children regularly enjoy masterclasses, all taking place in the Art Studio, a dedicated, light-filled space with a mezzanine area for our Scholars’ enrichment program. We also hold an annual exhibition of our Scholars’ work to much acclaim.
Beautifully curated, the standard and variety of work was breath-taking.

Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Design technology
Practical and future-focused, DT at Cumnor is designed for a fast-changing world where agility and creativity is key.
Under visionary leadership, DT at Cumnor has gone from strength to strength. We work with real life problems and projects relevant for today’s world – with sustainability in mind.
Housed in our dedicated STEM facility, our state-of-the-art DT lab is unrivalled in a prep school setting and is a hive of activity, innovation and creative confidence. With our open-door policy, pupils can drop in whenever they have a moment – so break times are never quiet!
Our DT program focuses on giving pupils the technical knowledge and skills to bring their ideas to life. Building their understanding of resistant materials, graphics, electronics and computer-aided design and manufacture using lasers, we give them the tools to innovate.
This practical, future-focused approach not only brings unusual agility in problem-solving to all our children. It has also brought the school significant scholarship success, too, with no less than five DT scholarships in the last year alone, to leading senior schools including Brighton College and King’s Canterbury.
Tori Bramly, Head of DT
A racing start
A racing start
Now a regular fixture in Cumnor’s STEM calendar, our annual go-kart project pits together teams of Year 6 pupils to dismantle and re-build a working kart, then test and race it. Challenging their scientific and mathematical knowledge throughout, the project culminates in a competitive race.
This year it was off to Goodwood to hone their driving skills as they competed in the drag race, slalom, chicane sprint, lap of champions and pit-stop challenge.

Destinations and scholarships
We are an outstanding school that produces dynamic and creative young people, well prepared and ready for their next steps, confident of who they are and what they can do.
We are proud to prepare our Year 8 leavers for a range of destination schools, including all of Sussex’s outstanding independent senior schools, and the very best weekly and full boarding schools across the country.

Sport at Cumnor
Regardless of ability, sport has the power to permeate us all. We believe that sport shapes character, builds community, and creates values that last a lifetime.
We are transforming what Prep school sport can look like. By inspiring every pupil to discover their individual opportunity, develop resilience, and lead with integrity — on and off the field — we are creating a programme that prioritises both enjoyment and excellence.
Our approach recognises that every child has different interests, strengths, and preferences, and we are committed to providing opportunities that ensure every moment is extraordinary. Through contemporary coaching methodologies, we nurture individual excellence within a supportive environment where every pupil can flourish. For those on an elite sporting pathway, our programme is centred around developing well-rounded, high-performing young athletes, with a strong emphasis on physical and psychological excellence.
Our teams have won a range of national and regional honours over the past five years and many of our children are linked into key regional pathways. Our approach has also seen our children secure a remarkable number scholarships to the top sporting senior schools in the country including Millfield, Tonbridge and Brighton College.
By embracing our vision and living our values, sport at Cumnor is enjoyable, inclusive, and developmental. By prioritising choice without compromising on standards, we inspire pupils to fully engage, challenge themselves, and embrace opportunities for growth.
Charlotte Collard-Rowe, Director of Sport
Sport for everyone
Sport for everyone
Ours is an inclusive, challenging, and rewarding sporting environment where all pupils are encouraged to pursue personal excellence, contribute meaningfully to their teams and enjoy the experiences and lessons that sport provides.
Sport is about more than competition — it is a journey of individual excellence and community pride.
For some this might mean competing at a regional or national level. For others it will be developing new skills and enjoying being part of a team.
Variety is key
Variety is key
Everyone is included. Guided by our expert staff, many of whom hold regional and national honours in their own right, all children will have regular opportunities to play, within school as well as externally in local and national events, festivals and fixtures. Needless to say, our Cumnor community will always be there, ready to support and celebrate our competitors.
Our range of sports include hockey, football, rugby, netball, cricket, tennis, golf, equestrian and athletics. Our broader options programme includes badminton, strength training, golf, hiking and dance.
Whatever the event, we are wholehearted in our participation, and we have a track record to show for it. Every pupil is part of an ongoing legacy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bursary Opportunities | Cumnor House Sussex
pageCache.text:
Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Bursary opportunities
We are delighted to offer the following bursaries – our Foundation Scholarships from Year 4 to Year 8 and our music tuition assistance, awarded in recognition of our commitment to the Performing Arts and musical excellence.
Foundation scholarships
Foundation scholarships
Through the Cumnor Foundation*, we fund bursaries – our Foundation Scholarships – which cover up to 100% of school fees and extras from Year 4 (aged 8+) to Year 8 (aged 13).
Applications are invited from local families for whom independent school education would otherwise be out of reach financially. Candidates should currently be in Year 3, performing towards the top of their class and curious to explore and deepen their talents, whether that be in the classroom, on the sports pitch or on the stage.
We help our bursary families to identify the best senior school for their child and facilitate this move for Year 9 entry, ideally with continued financial assistance at a similar level under that school’s own bursary programme.
Applications for Year 4 entry in September 2027 will open in December 2026 or January 2027.
*Charity No: 1168316
Music tuition bursary
Music tuition bursary
Children achieving the following grades are eligible to apply for paid tuition for up to two instruments, provided they are taught at the school. In the case of a music theory candidate achieving Grade 5, one of their instrumental studies at school will be supported. The Headmaster may also award discretionary financial assistance for music lessons to children in Year 3 to Year 5. These awards are reviewed annually.
Music Theory – Pass at Grade 5
